main_text.l: Materia generationis sic fuit in semi-ne, & sanguine menstruo: Membra generationis sunt vel communia, vel propria.
Suntq; vel praeparantia, vel conser-vantia semen.
Praeparantia sunt, quae semini materiam ex sanguinis seu ultimi alimenti portione & spiritu praeparant & elabo-rant.
Sunt autem vel longa, vel rotunda seu oblonga.
Longa sunt canales longi, partim a vena Cava, partim ab Aorta ad testes descendentes, paululum supra eos con-juncti & implicati.
Suntque cùm venæ, tùm arteriæ se-minales.
Venæ seminales sanguinem praeparant seu portionem ultimi alimenti semini cognatam excipiunt & deferunt. Sunt-que duae: Dextra à vena cavâ sub emul-gente

page.notes: The drop-cap M of "Materia" is a woodcut initial, read as M. The long s is transcribed as plain s throughout, including "semini" and "semen", which may be printed as "femini" and "femen". The catchword "gente" is partly cut off and is uncertain. The gathering signature at the foot is too faint to read and has been left out. The left-margin notes are transcribed as printed, including "Horū di-stinctio," which sits beside the Communia paragraph. The final line of the main text is cut off at the foot of the page, and the last word is the catchword.
